title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
summary_full: Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rightsCanada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.
